test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in 10 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. The pipe C can empty the tank in 30 minutes. All the three pipes are opened at a time in the beginning. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In what time, will the tank be full (in minutes)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work capacity = LCM(10, 20, 30) = 60 units.

Efficiencies of pipes A, B, and C are +6, +3, and −2 units/min respectively.

If outlet pipe C remained open for the last 2 minutes, it would empty 2 × 2 = 4 units.

Effective total work if all three pipes worked for the entire time = 60 − 4 = 56 units.

Total time = Effective total work ÷ Net efficiency = 56 ÷ (6 + 3 − 2) = 8 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A to fill the tank = 10 minutes

Time taken by pipe B to fill the tank = 20 minutes

Time taken by pipe C to empty the tank = 30 minutes

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (mins)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 10
 60

 20

 30
 −2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total time taken to fill the tank be x minutes.

⇒ Pipes A and B are open for the entire duration, so they work for x minutes.

⇒ Pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled, so it works for (x − 2) minutes.

⇒ Work done by A + Work done by B + Work done by C = Total Work

⇒ 6x + 3x − 2(x − 2) = 60

⇒ 9x − 2x + 4 = 60

⇒ 7x = 56

⇒ x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Pipes that fill the tank are assigned positive efficiency, while pipes that empty the tank are assigned negative efficiency. Net Efficiency = Sum of all active efficiencies.

Leaving Before Completion

If a worker (or pipe) stops working 'n' units of time before completion, add their potential work for those 'n' units to the total work, and assume everyone worked until the end. For outlet pipes, this means subtracting the work since they possess negative efficiency.

LCM Method for Time & Work

Assuming the total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual times avoids fractional calculations and significantly increases speed in competitive exams.
